gap: No result ChatGPT got puts a price on the stations whose makers document charging below freezing. Read today, the cheapest is the PECRON E1000LFP: $399 for 1,024 Wh ($0.39/Wh), charging down to -10°C (15°F on PECRON's page) with a battery heater that runs while it charges. The BLUETTI Pioneer Na is $700 for 900 Wh ($0.78/Wh, 5°F floor) and the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 is $949 for 1,536 Wh ($0.62/Wh, -4°F floor).
standout_why: Compared against runtimemath.com's cold limits for 18 models (updated 2026-11-16), energiasolarpro.com's cold-weather charging guide (cited in every chat), the Jackery FAQ pages and the Pioneer Na manual. runtimemath prices one model, the Elite 200 V2 ($899, which charges only above 32°F), and leaves out PECRON and the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra. energiasolarpro prices nothing and does not name the cheapest sub-freezing charger. ChatGPT showed PECRON E1000LFP and F5000LFP cards but gave no price, floor temperature or heater condition for them. No page sets price per Wh beside the charging floor. energiasolarpro also lists the Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus as a 32°F charger, while Jackery's own manual says -20°C.
decides: The pick depends on how cold it gets and how much the shopper wants to spend. Down to about 14°F, the PECRON E1000LFP is the cheapest maker-documented sub-freezing charger at half the Pioneer Na's price per Wh. Its heater needs live AC or DC input, so it does not help a pack that is cold-soaked with no input. From 14°F down to 5°F, the Pioneer Na is the only portable rated without a heater, but it charges only to 60% below 14°F. Down to -4°F, the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 at $949 is the cheapest in-stock unit rated that low (the 600 v2 is sold out). The HomePower 3600 Plus ($0.53/Wh) and DELTA Pro Ultra are for cabins and home backup. The usual LFP picks, including the Dealectric-listed Elite 200 V2, AC180, AC200L, DELTA 3 Plus, C1000 Gen 2 and Explorer 1000 v2, are all rated to charge only above 32°F.
